title: Mathematics achievement drill
description: Twelve curriculum questions at real ISEE pace, about fifty seconds each. This is the section that rewards knowing the material rather than spotting a trick. Four choices, and guessing costs nothing, so answer every one.

questions.explanation: The lowest common denominator of 6 and 4 is 12, giving 10/12 minus 3/12, which is 7/12. The choice 4/2 comes from subtracting tops and bottoms separately, which is never how fractions work.

questions.stem: What is the value of 3 + 4 x 2 squared?
questions.explanation: Order of operations: the exponent first, so 2 squared is 4, then multiply to get 16, then add 3 for 19. Choice B comes from multiplying before squaring, and choice C from adding first.
Subtract 2y from both sides to get 3y + 7 = 22, then subtract 7 to get 3y = 15, so y = 5. Move the variables to one side before the numbers and this stays tidy.

questions.stem: A recipe calls for 2 1/2 cups of flour. How much is needed for half the recipe?
questions.explanation: Half of 2 1/2 is 1 1/4. Turn it into 5/2 first if that helps, since half of 5/2 is 5/4. Choice D doubles the recipe instead of halving it.

questions.stem: What is the area of a triangle with a base of 10 and a height of 6?
questions.explanation: Area is half the base times the height, so half of 60 is 30. Choice C is what you get by forgetting the half, which is the single most common geometry slip on this test.

questions.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to 0.35?
questions.explanation: 0.35 is 35/100, which simplifies by 5 to 7/20. The choice 3/5 is 0.6 and 35/10 is 3.5, ten times too large.

questions.stem: The temperature was -4 degrees at dawn and rose 11 degrees by noon. What was it at noon?
questions.explanation: Starting at -4 and adding 11 crosses zero and lands on 7. Getting to zero uses 4 of the 11 degrees, leaving 7. Choice B subtracts instead of adding.

questions.stem: What is the perimeter of a regular hexagon with sides of length 7?
questions.explanation: Regular means all sides are equal, and a hexagon has six of them, so 6 times 7 is 42. Choice A treats it as a square and choice B as a pentagon, so the trap is miscounting the sides rather than the arithmetic.

questions.stem: If 4 notebooks cost $9.00, how much do 10 notebooks cost?
questions.explanation: One notebook is $2.25, so ten cost $22.50. Alternatively, ten is two and a half times four, and two and a half times $9.00 is $22.50. Choice A only doubles the price.

The mode is the value that appears most often, and 3 appears three times against two sevens. Choice C is roughly the mean and choice B is the median once sorted, so all three averages are represented here. Know which one is being asked for.

questions.stem: A map uses a scale of 1 inch to 25 miles. Two towns are 3.5 inches apart on the map. How far apart are they in reality?
questions.explanation: Multiply 3.5 by 25. Three inches is 75 miles and half an inch is 12.5, giving 87.5 miles. Splitting the multiplication into a whole part and a half is faster than long multiplication.

questions.stem: What is the value of x if the angles of a triangle measure x, 2x and 3x degrees?
questions.explanation: The three angles add to 180, and x plus 2x plus 3x is 6x, so 6x = 180 and x = 30. The angles are then 30, 60 and 90, which is why all three appear among the choices. Answering with the largest angle instead of x is the real risk here.
